newsitem.title: USA: Tiffany sees sparkling prospects - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Tiffany sees sparkling prospects - Barron's.

text.p: After three years of solid growth, Tiffany & Co chairman William Chaney sees sparkling prospects -- both domestically and internationally -- for its jewelry and other goods, according to an article in Barron's.
Chaney cited the strong economies in the U.S. and many other areas, especially the Asian Pacific Rim and Latin America, which are fueling affluence and demand for high-priced items.

Chaney's optimism is shared by many analysts on Wall Street, Barron's said. First Call reports a consensus estimate of $1.93 a share for fiscal 1997, which will end in January 1998. That would be more than 16 percent above fiscal 1996's $1.66 per share.

An argument for such bullishness is the performance of a store opened a year ago in Tokyo's plush Ginza district, Barron's said. Helped by the Tokyo store, Tiffany's retail sales in Japan have surged and Japan now represents well over 25 percent of the company's sales.

Tiffany's flagship Fifth Avenue store in New York remains the company's crown jewel however, still ringing up 17 percent of the retailer's total sales, Barron's said. A thriving tourist trade has been a consistent boost to the Fifth Avenue store.
